neighbours.label: 'says/speaks' used figuratively: a fact or act that reveals something about someone (that says a lot about, speaks well of)
fire: The fact that he returned the wallet says a lot about his character.
Her quiet loyalty to the team speaks volumes about her.
That the shop is still open after fifty years says something about its owners.
Honestly, the way they treat waiters says everything about them.
His decision to stay and help speaks well of him.
The size of the crowd at the funeral says much about how loved she was.
That nobody complained speaks to how well the event was run.
What a city chooses to build says a great deal about its values.
quiet: The man who returned the wallet says he found it on the bus.
Her coach says she will join the team next season.
The owner of the shop says it will close after fifty years.
Honestly, the waiter says the kitchen closes at ten.
During the meeting he speaks first and then answers questions.
At the funeral the priest says a short prayer for her.
Nobody complained, and the organiser speaks at the next event.
The mayor says the city will build a new bridge soon.

notes: Card: says, speaks, faces, 'What They Mean'; output of the + pole suppresses say/speak. Probe: 'says a lot about' 0.81, 'speaks well of' 0.80; literal 'says hello' 0.004, 'speaks French' 0.002. Tests meaning vs word.
